pullRequest.title: wsp-map#1235: a delete says gone only when the provider's reads agree
pullRequest.body:
Fixes https://github.com/wsp-labs/wsp-map/issues/1235

What it does: `killUntilGone`, the one read-back every provider delete goes through (wsp delete, init's builders and smoke forks, a failed create), no longer takes a single 404 as the machine gone. It wants twelve gone reads in a row, one call per read, asks for the delete up to three times, and asks again the moment a read finds the machine alive after a gone one. If the reads never agree inside three asks, the delete fails with the existing sentence naming the machine that is still running, and the record stays.

Why: on 2026-09-26 Solari's gateway copies disagreed call to call. One answered the delete with its usual 200 and the next read with 404 while another still answered the machine running, so wsp delete said gone and seven machines kept billing. The old read also spent two calls per poll (get, then state), so a read that reached the holder could still be decided by the next call landing on the empty copy.

Box by ASCII deletes through the same function and gets the same rule. A Solari or Box state its table does not know now reads running, never gone, through one `stateOf` helper in each backend.

Status: review rounds 1 and 2 fixed; head 9635c3e87. Build report and fix rounds are on the ticket.

commit.messageHeadline: fix(engine): a kill is done only when reads agree the machine is gone
commit.messageBody:
Solari's gateway copies disagreed call to call: one answered a delete
with its usual 200 and a read with 404 while another still answered the
machine running. killUntilGone took the first 404 as gone, so wsp delete
said gone and seven machines kept billing. It now wants twelve gone
reads in a row, one call each, asks up to three times, and asks again at
once when a read finds it alive; a state either backend never learned
reads alive.
No conflicts; both sides kept whole.

nodes.body:
Cold review of 9bfaa4d27 (ticket/1235) merged with origin/main 039a4d987 in a fresh detached worktree, fakes only, nothing sent to the real API.

## Gates
- `pnpm exec vitest run --minWorkers=1 --maxWorkers=2 packages/engine/test/solari-backend.test.ts packages/engine/test/box-backend.test.ts`: 119 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @wsp/engine exec tsc --noEmit`: exit 0.
- `packages/runtime/test/runtime.test.ts` with one worker: 334 passed, 2 failed on the missing wsp-daemon binary in a fresh worktree (create stages, verified wake). Both fail the same way with golden.ts at the base be94348a1, so they are the worktree's, not this diff's. The delete refusal tests at runtime.test.ts:403-500 pass under the new rule.
- Red-proof, golden.ts at the base: the three new tests fail (Box has 1 DELETE not 2; the Solari holder still has sb1; no MachineAliveError), 116 pass. Two-call read put back (`m.state()` in place of `seen.state`): the Box test and the "copies disagree on every read" test fail. Re-ask at once taken out (streak reset in place of the break): the Box test fails, the Solari "asks again" test still passes.

## Checked against the brief
- Fake gateway: the empty copy answers DELETE 200 and GET 404 and never held the id; the holder deletes only when a DELETE lands on it and reads 404 after. That is the shape the ticket measured, plus the 2026-09-04 note that a DELETE on an unknown id is 200.
- Callers: wsp delete (runtime.ts:5666) catches MachineAliveError, sets deleteSaid with the "after two asks" line and throws before drop(id), so the record stays. A failed create (runtime.ts:5338) reads a refusal as not gone and keeps the record. Init builders and failed seals (golden.ts:910 and :1268, sealGolden's kill at :993, :1008, :1025, :1067, :1068) catch or stage the left machine as before.
- The re-ask is the break at golden.ts:140 into the next pass of the same `attempt < 2` loop. Two asks at most; probe S3 below has a streak of four broken on the last ask end in MachineAliveError(running) with 2 deletes and 7 reads.
- Cost on a machine really gone: gone reads `continue` past the pollMs sleep, so five follow each other. Probe S1 against an instant fake with the default confirm: 1 ms, one DELETE, five GETs, every call naming /sandboxes/sb1. On Solari that is five round trips and nothing else.
- Failure line: `alive` is only ever assigned off a non-gone read, so the error names the provider's last word, never gone; the runtime wraps it as "x's machine <id> is still running after two asks; run wsp delete again or delete it at the provider".
- Box: DELETE 202 with GET running forever ends in MachineAliveError(running) after two asks (probe B1); 202 then 404s is done after five reads and one ask (probe B3); the PR's test pins 404, running, 404 as two deletes then exactly five GETs.
- Other ids: the loop only calls machine.kill() and backend.get(machine.id). A stale id the provider forgot (DELETE 404, GET 404) is done after one ask and five reads (probe S2). An id the provider hands to a new machine inside the read window is deleted by the second ask (probe S4); that is inherent in reading back by id, and the grace-window second ask already had it.

## Findings

SHOULD-FIX
1. golden.ts:111. `GONE_READS = 5` has no stated basis, and the ticket's own numbers point higher. Comment law: a constant states its constraint with the source; this comment cites the sweep's eight listings and then sets five without a word on why five is enough. Rough arithmetic from the ticket: seven of eleven deletes said gone wrongly under the old rule, which only needed the DELETE to miss the holder, so about two thirds of calls were landing on the copy that never held the machine. If calls land there independently with probability p between 0.65 and 0.7, a wrong gone under the new rule needs the ask to miss and five reads to miss, with one re-ask: p x (p^5 + (1 - p^5) x p x p^5), which is between one delete in eight and one in five. At eight reads it is between one in thirty and one in fifteen; at twelve, one in sixty or better. Each read is one round trip, about 0.3 s. Eleven samples and an independence assumption, so read the figures as a shape, not a measurement; the flipping listings support per-call routing but do not prove it. This wants a coordinator ruling on the number, and on whether extra asks are the cheaper lever (a DELETE on a gone machine is a harmless 200 on Solari and a 404 kill() already swallows on Box, and each one lands on the holder with probability 1 - p). Then one clause in the comment saying why the chosen number is enough.

NITS
2. solari-backend.test.ts:955. The title says "the read that finds it running asks again", but the test passes with the at-once re-ask taken out, because the grace-window second attempt also reaches two deletes. The Box test at box-backend.test.ts:943 is the only pin on the re-ask at once. One assertion that the second DELETE is the call right after the running read would let this test carry its own title. Test discipline.
3. PR body: "Status: draft until the build report is posted" is stale; the PR is ready and the report is on the ticket. Process law on PR bodies.
4. The build report's vitest gate ran with `--maxWorkers=2`; the builder gate in the skill is one worker. Process law on gates.

Notes, no severity
- box-backend.ts:125. STATE_MAP has no row for a box mid-delete; any GET state outside the map reads gone (`?? "gone"`) and satisfies the streak (probe B2 with a made-up "deleting" state: one DELETE, five GETs, done). Pre-existing and the same in state(), and the spike measured boxes gone from GET within seconds, so low risk; worth a row the day the provider answers such a state.
- Backends whose get() sets no seen (ssh, local) keep the two-call read through state(); one host answers there, so it is harmless. Probe N1 confirms the fallback runs one state() per read, five reads.

## Did well
- One rule in the one function every provider delete shares; Box gets it with no Box-only code, as the extension law wants.
- The fake gateway is a faithful model of the measured failure, and the one-call read is a real second cause the ticket did not name, found and fixed.
- The refusal keeps the record and names the provider's last word; a single alive read on the last ask refuses instead of waiting out the window, the right side to err on for a billing bug.
- Red-proofs are real: every new test fails on the base, and each fix line has a test that fails without it.
- The report says what it did not do, and the sweeps got their own ticket (#1285).

BLOCKERS (0) / SHOULD-FIX (1) / NITS (3)
- SHOULD-FIX golden.ts:111, GONE_READS unjustified against the ticket's own miss rate, comment law; coordinator ruling on the number.
- NIT solari-backend.test.ts:955, the test does not pin the at-once re-ask, test discipline.
- NIT PR body status line stale, process law.
- NIT gate ran with two workers, process law.

MERGE-AFTER-FIXES. The one should-fix is a ruling on a constant plus a comment clause, not a rework; if the coordinator rules that five stands, the comment clause alone closes it.

Re-review of fix round 1, head e8681dbfc (ticket/1235) merged with origin/main 56aeaf3a6 in a fresh detached worktree, fakes only, nothing sent to a provider.

## The last amend

`git diff d4454a3df e8681dbfc` is two comment lines at packages/engine/src/box-backend.ts:124-125 and nothing else. The builder's claim holds: the whole-suite gate at d4454a3df covers the code at the head.

## Gates
- `pnpm exec vitest run --minWorkers=1 --maxWorkers=2` on packages/engine/test/box-backend.test.ts, solari-backend.test.ts, golden.test.ts: 295 passed.
- packages/runtime/test/runtime.test.ts: 334 passed, 2 failed on the missing wsp-daemon binary in a fresh worktree; both pass with the binary copied in from a main checkout.
- packages/host/test/parity, skill, contract: 51 passed; contract's built-bin test wants dist/bin.js, which a fresh worktree has not built, and the diff touches no host source.
- `tsc --noEmit` on protocol, engine, runtime, host: exit 0.
- Red-proof, base golden.ts and box-backend.ts under the head's tests: all four new tests red, 116 pass. The re-ask `break` replaced by a streak reset: the Solari re-ask test times out at 5 s, so it now pins the at-once ask on its own.
- CI at e8681dbfc: four checks pass. Two workers on the gate is closed by the coordinator's brief.

## Round-1 findings, checked
1. golden.ts:111-112: `GONE_READS = 12`, `KILL_ASKS = 3`, the comment gives the measured skew and the one-in-sixty clause. The words follow: format.ts:1770 "after three asks", golden.ts:52 "after three kills", the `wsp delete` skill row, the three live tests' cleanup comments, golden.test.ts's three-kill timeline, runtime.test.ts reading `KILL_ASKS`. A grep for "two asks" and "two kills" finds nothing on the kill road.
2. solari-backend.test.ts:955: after the create the calls are exactly DELETE, GET, GET, DELETE, then twelve GETs under a 60 s grace. Verified red without the break.
3. PR body: no draft line, states twelve reads and three asks.
4. Box: `stateOf` at box-backend.ts:139 is the one helper; get() :529, list() :564 and state() :810 read through it, and no `?? "gone"` is left in the file. The new test covers the machine, the handle, the listing and the delete's refusal.

## The two questions
- No path believes a single 404. The only `return` in `killUntilGone` is `++gone >= GONE_READS`; `alive` is only ever assigned off a non-gone read; a read that fails for any reason but missing throws out. `wsp delete` (runtime.ts:5681) drops the record only after `unfork` resolves, and a `MachineAliveError` sets `deleteSaid` and rethrows before `drop`. A failed create (runtime.ts:5353) deletes its live entry only when `killUntilGone` resolved. The undriven branch kills once and drops, and that kind has no provider machine to bill.
- No path deletes a machine a record still claims: the loop calls `machine.kill()` and `backend.get(machine.id)` on the entry's own id and nothing else; the refusal keeps the record naming that id.

## Findings

SHOULD-FIX
1. packages/engine/src/solari-backend.ts:275 (and :294, :444, :457). `STATE_MAP[view.state] ?? "gone"`. The read `killUntilGone` now decides on is `seen.state` off get() at line 275, so a Solari state word outside the six the type declares reads gone and counts toward the streak; twelve of them drop the record with the machine still at the provider. This is the shape the round-1 ruling removed on Box, on the provider the ticket names, and it lives in four copies where Box has one helper (extension law: a rule is written once). The typed union covers Solari's documented states, so this is a defensive gap and not the measured one, which is why it is not a blocker. The ruling named Box alone, so whether it lands here or as a follow-up is the coordinator's call.

NITS
2. The two round-1 inline threads on this PR carry no builder reply with the sha and what changed; the fix round answers them on the ticket only. Process law: builders reply on PR threads, reviewers resolve.
3. The fix-round comment does not say whether a live run was repeated for the changed path. The skill's fix-round shape asks for that line; "not repeated, fakes only" would have done.

Notes, no severity, for a coordinator ruling
- runtime.ts:5701 `wsp forget` reads the machine once through `state()`, and one 404 drops the record. runtime.ts:7482 `forgetIfGone` reads the provider once and drops a builder's record on one 404. Neither kills a machine and neither is in this diff, but each is a record drop on a single 404 while the machine may still bill, and neither is one of #1285's sweeps.

## Did well
- One rule in the one function, the Box side through one helper, and no provider-specific branch above the backend.
- The re-ask test now carries its own title, with a grace window long enough that the old behaviour cannot pass by accident.
- The constants' comment states the measured basis in one clause, as the ruling asked, with no process words.
- Every claim in the fix round checked out against the code, including the "last amend is a comment reword" claim, which is the one that mattered for the gate.

BLOCKERS (0) / SHOULD-FIX (1) / NITS (2)
- SHOULD-FIX solari-backend.ts:275, :294, :444, :457: an unknown Solari state reads gone on the read the delete decides on; extension law and the round-1 Box ruling.
- NIT PR threads: no builder reply with the sha; process law.
- NIT fix-round comment: no live-run line; process law on fix rounds.

MERGE-AFTER-FIXES on the Solari fallback; MERGE as is if the coordinator rules that fallback a follow-up ticket.

Re-review of fix round 2, head 9635c3e87 (fix commit ed1c50670 plus merge of origin/main 56aeaf3a6) in a fresh detached worktree, fakes only, nothing sent to a provider.

## What changed since e8681dbfc

`git diff e8681dbfc ed1c50670` is two files: packages/engine/src/solari-backend.ts (14 lines) and packages/engine/test/solari-backend.test.ts (16 lines). The merge commit's tree is byte-identical to `git merge-tree --write-tree ed1c50670 56aeaf3a6`, so the merge brought nothing in by hand; "no conflicts, both sides kept whole" is verified, not trusted. Main's merged runtime.ts change is one import line; the PR touches no runtime source.

## Round-2 findings, checked

1. SHOULD-FIX, Solari's `?? "gone"` fallback. Fixed. One `stateOf` at solari-backend.ts:64, used at :266 (create reply), :279 (get), :298 (list), :448 (readState, the pause and resume fallback read) and :461 (state). `git grep '?? "gone"' -- packages/engine/src` is empty at the head. The only `STATE_MAP[` lookups outside a helper are Box's settle predicates (:508, :792) and the pause timeout words (:776), which compare against a known state and never decide gone. The typed `Record<SandboxView["state"], ...>` stays, so the six documented states remain exhaustive at compile time; the cast lives only inside the helper.
2. NIT, PR thread replies. Fixed: both round-1 threads carry a reply with the sha and what changed; neither is resolved.
3. NIT, live-run line. Present: not repeated, fakes only.

## Gates
- `pnpm exec vitest run --minWorkers=1 --maxWorkers=2` on packages/engine/test/box-backend.test.ts, solari-backend.test.ts, golden.test.ts: 296 passed (one more than round 1).
- packages/runtime/test/runtime.test.ts: 334 passed, 2 failed on the missing wsp-daemon binary in a fresh worktree; both pass with the binary copied in from a main checkout.
- packages/protocol/test/format.test.ts, packages/host/test/parity, skill, contract: 260 passed; contract's built-bin test wants dist/bin.js, which a fresh worktree has not built, and the diff touches no host source.
- `tsc --noEmit` on protocol, engine, runtime, host: exit 0 each.
- Red-proof: a throwaway worktree at e8681dbfc with the head's solari-backend.test.ts copied in fails exactly one test, the `archiving` one, with `expected 'gone' to be 'running'`; 62 pass. Green at the head.
- CI at 9635c3e87: four checks pass.

## The two questions
- No path believes a single 404: `killUntilGone` is unchanged since round 1; its only `return` is `++gone >= GONE_READS`, a missing read counts one toward the streak, and any other read failure throws out before a record is dropped. An unknown state word now counts as alive on every Solari and Box read, so it can only lengthen a delete, never shorten it.
- Nothing deletes a machine a record still claims: the loop kills and reads the entry's own id only, and the refusal keeps the record.

## Findings

NITS
1. Ticket comments, process law (rulings live on the ticket). The fix round says the Solari fallback landed "per the coordinator's ruling" and that `wsp forget` and `forgetIfGone` are "left out by ruling" and filed separately. No comment on wsp-map#1235 or on this PR carries either ruling; the last ruling on the ticket (02:13 UTC) names Box alone. The code stands on the round-2 review regardless, so this holds nothing: the coordinator posts the ruling as its own ticket comment, naming where the two record drops on a single 404 are filed.
2. packages/engine/test/solari-backend.test.ts:966, test discipline. The new test pins get, state and list, three of the five sites. readState at solari-backend.ts:448 is the one site where "running" changes an outcome outside delete: after a capped or network-failed resume, an unknown state word now reads as resumed and `resume()` returns, where before it threw `ResumeUnansweredError`. That is the right trade under the one-rule law (the next dial fails loudly, nothing is dropped, nothing bills unwatched), but a test on the resume fallback would make the choice deliberate rather than incidental. The create-reply site already fell back to running and is unreachable while the create reply carries no createdAt.

## Did well
- The self-review's grep found the fifth copy on the create reply, which the review had not named, and folded it in rather than leaving a second lookup shape.
- The helper's comment states the constraint and its reason in one clause with no process words, and matches Box's wording so the two backends read as one rule.
- The red-proof claim in the fix round reproduces exactly: same test, same message.
- The merge is a clean automatic merge and the commit message says so honestly instead of listing resolutions that did not happen.
- Every claim in the fix round checked out against the code and the PR threads.

BLOCKERS (0) / SHOULD-FIX (0) / NITS (2)
- NIT ticket comments: the round-2 rulings are cited but not posted; process law, coordinator's to post.
- NIT solari-backend.test.ts:966: readState (:448) untested; test discipline.

MERGE.
Landed on main as 3c48e16f8 by squash, in a train. Ticket: https://github.com/wsp-labs/wsp-map/issues/1235

SHOULD-FIX (comment law; needs a coordinator ruling on the number). Five has no stated basis and the comment above it cites eight. The ticket's seven of eleven wrong under the old rule means about two thirds of calls landed off the holder; at that rate five reads with one re-ask still let roughly one delete in eight to one in five say gone wrongly (rough, eleven samples, independence assumed). Eight reads: about one in thirty to one in fifteen. Twelve: one in sixty or better, at about 0.3 s a read. Extra asks are the other lever, since a DELETE on a gone machine is harmless on both providers. Whatever number is ruled, one clause here should say why it is enough. Full arithmetic in the review body.

Fixed in d4454a3df (now in ed1c50670, merged with main at 9635c3e87): `GONE_READS = 12` and `KILL_ASKS = 3` per the coordinator ruling on wsp-map#1235, and the comment gives the measured skew and the one-in-sixty clause. The failure lines now say three asks and three kills.

NIT (test discipline). This passes with the at-once re-ask replaced by a streak reset, because the grace-window second attempt also reaches two deletes; only the Box test pins the re-ask at once. Asserting that the second DELETE is the call right after the running read would make the title true of this test alone.

Fixed in d4454a3df (now in ed1c50670, head 9635c3e87): the test runs with a 60 s grace window and asserts DELETE, GET, GET, DELETE, then `GONE_READS` GETs after the create. With the break replaced by a streak reset, it times out.
